frozen_candidate_root_contribution: To take the side of a party in a contest or jeopardy and actively back it against an opponent or threat - partisan aid on that party's behalf, oriented toward its deliverance or prevailing (victory/redress). The backing is the act/offer itself: it may be present, sought, refused, rendered-yet-failed, or impossible, and guaranteed success attaches only when the backer is God.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: To take the side of a party in a contest or jeopardy and actively back it against an opponent or threat - partisan aid on that party's behalf, oriented toward its deliverance or prevailing (victory/redress). The backing is the act/offer itself: it may be present, sought, refused, rendered-yet-failed, or impossible, and guaranteed success attaches only when the backer is God.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across the verbal and nominal derivations (form I naSara, verbal noun naSr, agent/intensive nouns naaSir/naSiir/anSaar, patient manSuur, plus reciprocal VI tanaaSara, self-directed VIII intaSara, and requestative X istanSara) the root names partisan backing of a side against an adversary or danger. This is tighter than generic 'help': every instance carries an opponent, enemy, threat, or oppression, and the Quran keeps naSr distinct from provision (rizq), guidance (hidaayah), standing patronage (walii), and deflecting harm (Sarf). The proper-noun class naSaaraa/naSraaniyy ('the Christians') shares only the consonantal skeleton and is a separate lexicalized lexeme with no recoverable Quran-internal link to backing.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: nSr does NOT entail: (a) generic help/provision/benefaction - it is always adversarial/partisan, and naSr is enumerated separately from rizq in 8:26; (b) guidance - separately enumerated from naSiir in 25:31; (c) standing guardianship/patronage - the fixed doublet 'walii ... naSiir' (16+ times, e.g. 2:107) keeps guardian distinct from defender; (d) deflecting/averting harm (Sarf) - distinguished from naSr in 25:19; (e) success itself - backing can be rendered and still fail (59:12) and idols cannot even back themselves (21:43, 36:75); (f) naSr is not fatH - they are paired as complementary (110:1, 61:13). Form-VIII adds a retributive/redress component (redress from a wrongdoer) not carried by the bare nucleus.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The proper-noun class naSaaraa/naSraaniyy (15 occ, e.g. 22:17 in a bare enumeration of religious communities with al-Saabiiiin/al-majuus, and 3:67 'Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian'). No sense of aid/helper/victory/redress can be substituted; the argument structure that carries the nucleus everywhere else (beneficiary, adversary, min/alaa complement) is structurally absent. The Quran never internally derives or glosses naSaaraa from 'helping' - when it means 'helpers of God/Jesus' it uses a different lexeme, anSaar (3:52, 61:14). Any link is external etymology, which is disallowed. This is decisive proof that same-root does not equal one meaning here and caps the root against a single nucleus.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: That the nucleus is martial 'victory/prevailing' (outcome-state), with 'help' as its causative - anchored in naSru-llaahi wa-l-fatH (110:1), naSran aziizan (48:3), and the manSuuruun/ghaalibuun pairing (37:171-172). Rejected because the verb overwhelmingly encodes the RELATION of backing a party, not a bare outcome: imperatives (unSurnaa alaa, 2:250), conditionals (in tanSuruu-llaaha yanSurkum, 47:7), the walii doublet, idols that cannot back even themselves (21:43), the juridical vindication of 17:33, the generalized eschatological rescue (laa yunSaruun), and forms VI/X/VIII are not martial victories. Above all 59:12 shows naSr given yet victory withheld - victory is the frequent RESULT of divine naSr, not its meaning. The over-broad 'generic help' gloss is also rejected: the four neighbour-contrasts (rizq, hidaayah, walaayah, Sarf) show the Quran keeps naSr distinct from adjacent aid-concepts.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses converge: one dominant, coherent derivational family (~143/158) meaning partisan backing against an opponent/threat, plus one unbridged lexicalized proper-noun class (naSaaraa/naSraaniyy, 15). Considered alone the backing family is broad, distinctive and adversarially clean - spanning form I in all moods/voices, the verbal noun, naSiir/naaSir/anSaar/manSuur/ADJ, and forms VI/VIII/X - with a text-internal minimal pair (26:93 yanSuruunakum [other] vs yantaSiruun [self]) grammaticalizing the I-vs-VIII split. That portion would tempt STRONG. But two contract triggers cap it at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE: (i) a resistant lexicalized nominal sub-class exists - the PN naSaaraa (15 occ, ~10%) not bridged on internal evidence; and (ii) form VIII carries a materially shifted retributive/redress sense (avenge/take redress after Zulm: 26:227, 42:41, 47:4). The nucleus is therefore derivationally unified but not uniformly one meaning across all 158 tokens; the PN link is retained as UNRESOLVED rather than forced into a bridge.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form I naSara/yanSuru (perfect, imperfect, imperative, passive): other-directed backing of a party against an adversary or threat, prototypically God backing believers to victory/deliverance, but also humans backing God's cause; the passive laa yunSaruun = to be left unbacked/defenceless.
clusters.classification_rationale: Stable argument frame: accusative beneficiary + adversary via min (11:30 'who backs me against God') or alaa (2:250 'back us against the disbelievers'); reciprocity in 47:7 (in tanSuruu-llaaha yanSurkum); telos of prevailing shown by ghaalibiin outcomes and opposition to khadhala (3:160). The passive concentrates in the Judgment refrain (rescue withheld).
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 3:123:2:1 (Badr), 21:77:1:2 (deliverance min al-qawm), 11:30:3:1 (min Allah), 47:7:5:1 (humans back God), 59:12:16:1 (backing rendered yet fails), 2:250:12:2 (petition unSurnaa).

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Deverbal/agent/patient nouns of backing: naSr (the backing / granted victory, paired with fatH), naSiir & naaSir & anSaar (backer/defender/ally/helpers), manSuur (one authoritatively backed/vindicated), and attributive ADJ naSiir (17:80 'a backing authority'). All express the same partisan-backing role.
clusters.classification_rationale: naSiir locked in the walii doublet (2:107 etc.) marks the defender-role adjacent to but distinct from the guardian; naaSir overwhelmingly negated ('they have no backer'); anSaar the concrete helper-cohort incl. 'helpers of God' (3:52, 61:14); naSr explicitly 'only from God' (3:126) and paired with fatH (110:1); manSuur the backed/vindicated party (37:172, 17:33). Idol impotence (21:43, 36:75) confirms naSr is the act/offer of backing, not guaranteed success.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Regular valence operations on the nucleus: VI tanaaSara = render mutual backing (37:25 'why do you not back one another'); X istanSara = seek/request backing (28:18 'the one who sought his aid'; 8:72 'if they seek your backing in the religion').
clusters.classification_rationale: Both are transparent derivational operations (reciprocal, desiderative) on form I with no semantic shift beyond valence.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form VIII intaSara / muntaSir: the backing turned on oneself - defend oneself / secure victory for oneself, with a systematic RETRIBUTIVE specialization 'take redress / avenge oneself after being wronged' (intaSara min X = exact redress from a wrongdoer). Bridgeable to the nucleus as securing naSr for oneself, but carrying a redress component the bare nucleus lacks.
clusters.classification_rationale: Clusters with Zulm/baghy: 26:227 (redress after being wronged), 42:39 (redress when baghy strikes), 42:41 (redress after one's wrong), 47:4 (would have taken redress from them); neutral middle 'defend oneself' in 26:93/18:43/51:45/54:44/55:35. The min-complement here marks the TARGET of vengeance, not the threat protected-against as in form I - a genuine derivational sub-sense, not mere morphological variation.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 26:93:7:1 (minimal pair vs form I), 54:10:5:2 (Noah: fa-ntaSir), 18:43:11:1 & 51:45:7:1 (muntaSir, incapacity).

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Lexicalized proper noun naSaaraa (the Christians) / naSraaniyy (a Nazarene): a fixed ethno-religious communal label, listed beside al-yahuud, al-Saabiiiin, al-majuus, al-mushrikuun. No backing/help/victory/redress sense operates; an inert homograph of the root consonants, unbridged on Quran-internal evidence.
clusters.classification_rationale: Never governs a help-object, never verbalized, QAC-tagged PN throughout; appears in bare enumerations (22:17) and as an individual affiliation descriptor (3:67 'neither Jew nor Christian') where no sense of aid can be substituted. When the Quran means 'helpers of God/Jesus' it uses the distinct lexeme anSaar (3:52, 61:14) and separately names the community naSaaraa. Any link to the backing nucleus would require external etymology, which the source policy forbids.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 22:17:7:3, 3:67:6:1, 2:113:4:2, 5:82:18:1, 9:30:7:2 - all fixed communal-label usages with no backing semantics.

reconciliation.rationale: Form VIII regularly turns the backing on the self; intaSara-min is 'secure naSr for oneself against a wrongdoer'. The redress coloring is a derivational specialization, so the occurrence stays within the nucleus rather than forming a separate class.
The nucleus is 'partisan backing so the party's cause prevails', not 'battlefield victory'; juridical backing of a rightful claim is an instance, and it usefully bars the narrow martial competitor.

adversarial_verification.notes: A full adversarial refutation cannot return PASSED because a coherent resistant lexicalized sub-class (the PN naSaaraa) persists unbridged; the backing nucleus itself survives every form-I/nominal/VI/VIII/X occurrence with clean neighbour-contrasts, so the core is not FAILED. Per contract, some occurrences resist while the core holds - status is NOT_RUN with the resistant occurrences recorded.

independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A bottom-up, B derivational, C adversarial) converged on the same two-class result (one backing family + one unbridged PN class) and the same MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE grade.
candidate_root_contribution: To take the side of a party in a contest or jeopardy and actively back it against an opponent or threat - partisan aid on that party's behalf, oriented toward its deliverance or prevailing (victory/redress). The backing is the act/offer itself: it may be present, sought, refused, rendered-yet-failed, or impossible, and guaranteed success attaches only when the backer is God.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 158 occurrences read in full; form I verb (59) and nominal family naSr/naSiir/naaSir/anSaar/manSuur (69) + ADJ (1) show a stable adversarial backing frame (min/alaa complements, walii doublet, idol impotence, given-yet-failed backing in 59:12).
layer_attribution.derivation: Forms VI (tanaaSara, mutual), VIII (intaSara, self-directed with retributive shift), and X (istanSara, requestative) are regular valence operations on the form-I nucleus; the 26:93 minimal pair (yanSuruunakum vs yantaSiruun) grammaticalizes the other-vs-self split.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: The proper-noun class naSaaraa/naSraaniyy (15) is a lexicalized ethno-religious label sharing only the consonantal skeleton, carved out as a separate lexeme; manSuur is the patient noun of backing and belongs to the nucleus.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Divine victory, fatH, and battlefield outcome (Badr 3:123, ghaalibiin) are narrative/contextual RESULTS of divine naSr, not the verb's meaning; they must not be promoted into the root claim, which is the relation of partisan backing itself.

reopen_conditions: If a Quran-internal statement is found deriving naSaaraa/naSraaniyy from helping (e.g. tying al-naSaaraa to anSaar/naSr within the text rather than by external etymology), re-examine whether the PN class C5 bridges into the backing nucleus and the scope should rise.

If form-VIII intaSara occurrences (26:227, 42:41, 47:4) are judged to constitute a distinct redress lexeme rather than a derivational specialization, reopen whether C4 should be split from the nucleus as its own class.
